speeding.why: Speed decides how much time you have to react and how hard a crash is; examiners fail clear overspeeding.
speeding.how: Check the speedometer after every sign and junction; lift off early and hold the limit instead of catching up.
speeding.drill: Drive one route checking the speedometer at every limit sign and staying under it.

red_light.why: Running a red light is a major fault that fails the exam and causes side-impact crashes.
red_light.how: Treat amber as a stop signal: cover the brake when approaching junctions and stop at the line.
red_light.focus: Stopping for red and amber lights
red_light.drill: Approach signal-controlled junctions with your foot covering the brake and stop at the line on amber.

stop_sign.why: At a STOP sign the car must stop completely at the line; rolling through is an exam fault.
stop_sign.how: Brake progressively so the car stops fully before the line, hold the stop for a second, then look both ways.
stop_sign.drill: Practise full stops at the line at several STOP signs, holding each stop for a full second.

pedestrian_crossing.why: Pedestrians on a crossing have priority; not yielding endangers the most vulnerable road users.
pedestrian_crossing.how: Scan both pavements as you approach a crossing, slow down early and stop if anyone is waiting or crossing.
pedestrian_crossing.drill: On a route with crossings, slow down before each one and say out loud whether anyone is waiting.

wrong_way.why: Driving against the traffic on a one-way street risks a head-on collision and fails the exam.
wrong_way.how: Look for one-way and no-entry signs before turning and plan the route in advance.
wrong_way.drill: Before each turn, name the sign that allows it; practise in the narrow Old City streets.

give_way.why: Not giving way forces others to brake or swerve and is a major exam fault.
give_way.how: Slow down before the give-way line, check traffic on the priority road and go only when it is clear.
give_way.drill: At every give-way junction, slow to walking pace and check both directions before entering.

collision.why: A collision is a major fault and shows the car was not under control for the situation.
collision.how: Leave more space, slow down near obstacles and look further ahead so you can stop within the distance you can see.
collision.focus: Space and speed control near obstacles
collision.drill: Drive in free mode keeping a generous gap and slowing before every parked car or tight turn.

landing.title: Learn to drive in Baku before you take the wheel
landing.lead: Drive real Baku streets under real Azerbaijani traffic rules. After every drive, an AI instructor explains exactly what happened, which rule it was, and what to practise next.
landing.heroAlt: Roadwise debrief: the instructor's summary, issues linked to the moment they happened, and the next drill
landing.problemTitle: A fine tells you what. It does not tell you why.
landing.problemBody: Learner drivers practise for hours but get little feedback they can act on. A list of fines does not say which habit caused them, which mistake would fail the exam, or whether you are getting better.

how.title: Drive
how.body: Free drive or a checkpoint exam through central Baku. The examiner checks red lights, STOP lines, crossings, one-way streets, giving way, speed and collisions — and records what you did right too.

how.title: Debrief
how.body: Roadwise measures the drive itself: rules followed, time over the limit, harsh braking, steering. The AI instructor explains those numbers, cites the exact moment and rule, and plans your next drive.

how.title: Progress
how.body: Your profile tracks every drive, compares it with the previous ones and shows an exam-readiness score with a full breakdown of how it was calculated.

shots.readiness: An exam-readiness score you can audit, point by point.
shots.progress: Progress across drives: rules followed, composure, fines.

landing.rulesTitle: Real Baku streets. Real Azerbaijani rules.
landing.rulesLead: The city is built from OpenStreetMap data and enforces right-hand traffic. Fines follow the rates of the Azerbaijani Administrative Offences Code (İXM); some are still provisional.
landing.bandNote: Speeding: +11–20 km/h 10 AZN · +21–40 50 AZN · +41–60 200 AZN (major) · +61 or more 300 AZN (major).
honest: Every number comes from measured drive data, never from the AI.
Each debrief is checked against the drive before you see it; if it does not pass, you get a plain template instead of a guess.
Composure is estimated from driving signals — it does not measure stress.
landing.finalBody: Create an account, download the game and log in from it in under a minute.

download.title: Download Roadwise
download.lead: The desktop game is free. Your progress lives in your Roadwise account.
download.unavailable: The download link is not configured yet.
download.unsignedBody: Early builds are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen or macOS may show a warning. On Windows choose More info → Run anyway; on macOS right-click the app and choose Open.
steps: Open Roadwise and press Log in. Your browser opens with a short code.
Log in to the website (or create an account) and click Authorise this device.
Return to the game — it says Signed in as your name. Every drive now uploads to your profile.
